newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amalia shares leap on Liberia mining deal.
newsitem.headline: Amalia shares leap on Liberia mining deal.

text.p: Shares in Amalia Gold Mining & Exploration Co Ltd rose sharply late on Tuesday following news that its Commonwealth Gold (Comgold) arm had signed a deal with Liberia to develop its mining resources.
Shares touched a high of 160 cents in afternoon trade, a jump of 21 percent or 28 cents. By 1440 GMT shares had come off their highs to trade at 148 cents -- a gain of 16 cents.
The agreement between Comgold subsidiary, The Resource and General Finance Corp of West Africa, and the government of Liberia was signed on June 16 but the news was only released on Tuesday.
Comgold will hold 40 percent of joint venture concern, Liberia Resources Corp (LibeResCo), and the government 60 percent.
"LibeResCo holds all the rights to develop Liberia's gold, diamond, iron ore, bauxite and offshore oil and gas," Comgold said in a statement.

"The company will be listed on the London Stock Exchange in three to four years by which time the main shareholders expect it to have a market capitalisation of $5 billion," the company added, without giving a valuation breakdown.

Apart from the iron ore mines, which were the world's third largest supplier of iron ore until 1989, when an eight-year civil war disrupted the industry, Liberia's mining sector is largely underdeveloped.
In another development, Comgold said it is to partially unbundle its shareholding in its Holistic Resources unit and seek to list the firm on the South African bourse and an international exchange.
The Liberia deal would see Holistic's market value leap from the reintroduction of official trading in Liberian gold and diamonds.
